answers.explanation: The default source grid is the exact public 7x5 board. parse() derives player, boxes, goals and walls from that grid; the independent reject-chain fixture starts player [1,1], boxes [2,1]/[3,1], goals [5,1]/[6,1].

Wall/chain-blocked pushes are rejected before mutating player, boxes or tick. The captured ArrowRight chain rejection preserves the entire observed state and emits no events. Restart is checked separately below.
A successful push emits one PUSH event, then WIN only when all goals are occupied. The independently authored final-goal fixture and captured record agree on PUSH then WIN, each once.

Rejected wall/chain push has an empty event list and unchanged state; the captures show no spurious PUSH/WIN. Restart emits no semantic event. Observed event multiplicity/order matches the declared rules.

Terminal is set after an accepted push fills every goal; final-goal fixture records won/all_goals_filled with WIN. Further directional input is rejected while terminal; restart clears terminal and restores the initial state.

The captured sequence wins, restarts to initial state with terminal null, and wins again; this supports arrow input, restart, occupancy and authoritative terminal feedback. No unmet task-specific terminal obligation found.
The DOM keydown listener maps arrow keys and R/P to step actions, prevents default, and records transitions; a real captured ArrowRight reaches terminal.
Captured restart trace shows action sequence right, restart, right; state resets player/box/tick/terminal. The evidence covers Arrow keys and restart; no pointer control is required by this task.

I viewed all three supplied FPS screenshots: each visibly renders a bounded grid, player, two boxes and two goal markers, with arrow/restart/pause guidance. main.mjs retains goal-cell class while drawing overlays.

The source adds win feedback only from snapshot terminal state, and the captured final-goal record text contains “All goals filled!”. Supplied screenshots cover initial visual state at all rates, not a distinct won screenshot; terminal rendering is supported by source plus captured text.
